requirement: Describe the single-site randomized parallel-arm superiority trial of patient-support-person dyads comparing FAM-ACT with individually focused diabetes self-management education and support.

evidence.text: The abstract and design overview define the dyadic randomized parallel comparison and name both interventions.

requirement: Randomize dyads 1:1 to FAM-ACT or I-DSMES and, before finalization, specify sequence generation, any stratification or blocking, allocation concealment and implementation roles.

evidence.text: The protocol states 1:1 dyad randomization and electronic return of assignment but omits the sequence-generation and concealment details.

requirement: Preserve assessor blinding: research associates conducting outcome assessments are blinded, while participants, support persons and intervention providers are not.

evidence.text: The SAP explicitly distinguishes blinded outcome assessors from unblinded participants, support persons and care providers.

requirement: Represent the COVID adaptation: the first 77 dyads followed the original 12-month intervention, later dyads followed a 6-month intervention, and outcomes may be observed at baseline, 6 months and when available 12 months.

evidence.text: The protocol documents the March-2020 disruption, the original 77 dyads, the February-2021 adapted protocol and both assessment horizons.

requirement: Define the enrolled unit as an adult patient with type 2 diabetes and poor glycemic or blood-pressure control plus one unpaid English- or Spanish-speaking support person meeting the protocol eligibility criteria.

evidence.text: The eligibility section defines patient and support-person inclusion and exclusion criteria.

requirement: Distinguish FAM-ACT's joint patient-support-person introduction, family-focused education and dyadic community-health-worker contacts from I-DSMES's patient-focused introduction, standard education and patient contacts.

evidence.text: The two program sections specify the shared and arm-specific intervention components.

requirement: Analyze assessments at baseline and 6 months for all adapted-protocol participants and use 12-month measures only where collected under the original or extended follow-up schedule.

evidence.text: The design and arm descriptions establish the core and conditional follow-up measurements.

requirement: Define the primary endpoint as between-arm difference in change in patient HbA1c percentage from baseline to 6 months.

evidence.text: The abstract and Aim 1 name 6-month HbA1c change as the primary outcome.
The SAP defines the endpoint scale and randomized contrast.

requirement: Cover secondary changes in HbA1c and blood pressure, diabetes distress, self-care, self-efficacy, activation and perceived support at their protocol-defined 6- or 12-month time points.

evidence.text: The aims and measures tables identify the secondary outcome families and collection times.

requirement: Document 268 dyads, 134 per arm, based on detecting a 0.6 percentage-point 6-month HbA1c difference with at least 80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05, SD 1.75%, within-patient ICC 0.6 and 20% attrition.

evidence.text: The power table and accompanying text provide the model assumptions, evaluable target and attrition inflation.

requirement: Use the intention-to-treat population as primary, retaining randomized patients according to assigned intervention regardless of noncompliance or delivery changes.

evidence.text: The primary-analysis and intercurrent-event sections state ITT and treatment-policy handling.

requirement: Analyze repeated HbA1c at baseline, 6 months and 12 months with a linear mixed-effects model containing time, intervention arm and their interaction, and test the primary 6-month effect with a linear contrast.

evidence.text: The primary-analysis section gives the repeated-measures model and confirmatory contrast.

requirement: Adjust the primary model for baseline HbA1c, patient-support-person co-residence, baseline insulin use and age, prioritizing baseline HbA1c if it is highly correlated with insulin use and moving insulin use to sensitivity analysis.

evidence.text: The SAP names all covariates and the priority rule for correlated HbA1c and insulin use.

requirement: Use two-sided alpha 0.05 and report treatment effects with 95% confidence intervals; make clear that secondary, mediation and moderation analyses are hypothesis-generating and receive no multiplicity adjustment.

evidence.text: The general and primary methods state alpha, interval reporting and the no-adjustment rationale.

requirement: Analyze continuous secondary outcomes analogously to the primary model and categorical or ordinal secondary outcomes with generalized linear mixed models using a logit link and time-specific linear contrasts.

evidence.text: The secondary-endpoint section specifies analogous models, GLMMs and time-specific contrasts.

requirement: Treat the prespecified baseline HbA1c, insulin use, sex, co-residence, support-person diabetes, disease duration, health literacy, baseline support and pre/during-COVID subgroup analyses as exploratory interaction analyses.

evidence.text: The moderator section lists the subgroups and group-by-time interaction approach.

requirement: For exploratory mediation, estimate average direct and indirect effects with natural-effect models using ratio-of-mediator-probability weights and a marginal structural outcome model.

evidence.text: The SAP describes counterfactual mediation, dataset expansion, RMPW and the marginal structural model.

requirement: Summarize missingness by outcome, arm and site, compare baseline characteristics of complete versus incomplete cases, state the mixed-model MAR assumption and use multiple imputation where required by the intercurrent-event strategy.

evidence.text: The analytical-issues section defines missingness summaries, MAR and multiple imputation.

requirement: Implement the SAP's primary strategies for home rather than clinic HbA1c, phone rather than in-person surveys, widened assessment windows, noncompliance, delayed classes, Zoom delivery and support-person changes, with supplementary hypothetical or principal-stratum analyses as specified.

evidence.text: The intercurrent-event table enumerates each event and its primary and supplemental strategies.

requirement: Assess departures from MAR with a control-based MNAR imputation in which missing FAM-ACT outcomes are imputed from the I-DSMES control-arm distribution.

evidence.text: The sensitivity section prespecifies control-based imputation for MNAR robustness.

requirement: Estimate a supplementary complier average causal effect using randomized assignment as an instrumental variable, with the arm-specific attendance definition and a patient-attendance-only sensitivity definition.

evidence.text: The SAP defines instrumental-variable CACE and both compliance definitions.

requirement: Assess COVID-period effects by comparing recruitment and enrolled characteristics before versus from March 2020 and by testing an intervention-by-COVID-period interaction, reporting period-stratified effects if heterogeneous.

evidence.text: The COVID impact section defines period comparisons and the heterogeneity model.

requirement: Before finalization, define serious-adverse-event summaries by randomized patient arm, CTCAE category, relatedness and study period, and state the correct patient and support-person denominators.

evidence.text: The data and safety plan defines adverse-event collection, CTCAE categorization, adjudication and reporting but not the analysis summaries.
